DIAGNOSIS READY: Phyllodes Tumor (likely Benign or Malignant)

The rapid growth of a discrete breast mass in a 48-year-old patient, especially if imaging suggests it is well-circumscribed but potentially mobile or fixed, strongly suggests a Phyllodes tumor rather than a typical fibroadenoma or carcinoma. Please confirm if you have a family history of breast cancer or previous breast surgeries, and describe the exact appearance of the mass on the ultrasound (e.g., leaf-like architecture).
